title: NOx next-hour prediction - Italy (UCI Air Quality)
summary: We predicted NOx one hour ahead using the Italy (UCI Air Quality) data. Random Forest did best on the validation period, so we used it. On the test period (16 Jan 2005 to 4 Apr 2005) its average error was 57.562 ppb. Just repeating the last hour's value gave 72.734 ppb, so the model was 20.9% better. 25 episodes were flagged: 10 look like unusual pollution, 12 look like data problems and 3 are unclear.
how_it_was_made: Read the hourly data and treated empty cells and -200 as missing.

Built the inputs: hour, weekday, the reading 1 hour before, the reading 2 hours before, the reading 3 hours before, the reading at the same time the day before, temperature, relative humidity, absolute humidity.
Split the timeline in order: first 60% to train, next 20% to choose the model, last 20% to test.
Tried Linear Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost. Each predicts how much the level changes in the next hour.
Flagged test hours where the miss was more than 269.90 ppb (bigger than 95% of the misses on the validation period).
By design this limit flags 5% of the validation hours; on the test period it flagged 1.6% of hours. So the number of episodes partly depends on where the limit is set.

Grouped flagged hours that were less than 3 hours apart and checked each group: missing inputs or a gap, a stuck reading, or a sudden jump that nothing else shared mean a data problem; other pollutants moving the same way at the same time mean unusual pollution; anything else is unclear.
patterns: Most episodes peaked around 08:00, 20:00 and 21:00, and 80% fell on weekdays, more than the 71% you'd expect, so they lean towards working days. The busiest month was Feb 2005 with 11 episodes.

most_severe.explanation: Mon 17 Jan 2005, 18:00 to 20:00: NOx was 582.00 ppb at 20:00, but the model expected about 1095.05 ppb, so it was 513.05 lower. The inputs were complete, and CO, NO2 and C6H6 were also unusually low at the same time. These come from separate instruments, so this looks like a real drop in pollution.
